title: Unraveling the multifaceted influences of environmental conditions and additives on highland oat silage: a comprehensive study of nutritional, molecular, and ruminal degradation properties
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Exploring and establishing appropriate fermentation conditions is critical for enhancing the quality of silage in high-altitude regions. This study evaluated the effects of different environmental conditions and additives on the nutritional value, molecular structure, and ruminal degradation parameters of oat silage. A total of 72 forage bags were assigned to 12 treatments (3 additives × 4 environments). Additives included lactic acid bacteria (LAB), organic acids (OA), and a control (CON). Environmental conditions were low-altitude ambient (LA), high-altitude ambient (HA), high-altitude glasshouse (HG), and high-altitude constant temperature (HC). All samples were ensiled for 42 days before analysis.

RESULTS

The LA group exhibited the highest levels of lactic acid, acetic acid and ammonia-nitrogen (NH3-N). LAB treatment yielded the highest acetic acid levels, while OA treatment showed the highest NH3-N (P < 0.05). For nutritional fractions, the HC group had the lowest non-fiber carbohydrates (P < 0.05). The LA group had the highest ammonia content (P < 0.05). OA treatment reduced the neutral-detergent fiber and acid-detergent insoluble protein contents more than CON and LAB treatments, while the LAB treatment had the lowest ammonia content (P < 0.05). Correlation analysis showed carbohydrates positively correlated with the peak height of total carbohydrate sub-peak II. The heights of the amide I region, α-helix, and β-sheet, were positively correlated with crude protein and soluble protein contents. For ruminal fermentation parameters, the HG group showed the highest volatile fatty acids concentrations (P < 0.05).

CONCLUSION

OA improves oat silage quality under HA condition, whereas high-quality fermentation could be achieved without additives under HG condition. © 2025 Society of Chemical Industry.
